items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear and the public APIs have doc comments. But `var sentinelVal int; var defaultBatchDurable = func(BatchDurableInfo){ sentinelVal++ }`, compared by reflect pointer, is an obscure hack with no comment. Two near-identical BatchDurableInfo blocks in applyInternal make it hard to read. No String/SafeFormat on the info struct.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: durability.go is 523 lines, over the cap. applyInternal grows by about 80 lines, with two copy-pasted info-building blocks and a nested goroutine. It uses global mutable `sentinelVal` and a reflect.ValueOf(f).Pointer() sentinel check. The durability logic leaks into db.go instead of being fed from commit.go.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Errors latch and waiters unblock on close, and the limits are named constants. However, `sentinelVal++` runs unsynchronized on every concurrent Sync commit when no listener is set, which is a data race. Each NoSyncWait commit also spawns its own goroutine. The final `return ctx.Err()` relies on ctx being non-nil.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The APIs are additive. But every Sync commit now takes a mutex and allocates a jobState plus a channel in allocateJobID, even when BatchDurable is unset. NoSyncWait commits now spawn a goroutine and Ref the batch. Options.Clone now deep-copies EventListener, a small change in behaviour.
